H1_per_row_vold.claim: Per-row frozen V_old encode plus .item() synchronisation is a major learner bottleneck.
H1_per_row_vold.evidence: 753 vold_encode calls = 5430 ms (23.2% of learner); vold_item only 79 ms (0.3%); vold_obs 1011 ms (4.3%).
H1_per_row_vold.detail: The per-row ENCODE is real and large (23% of learner). But the hypothesised .item() synchronisation is negligible (0.3%), so the cost is per-call kernel latency, not host sync. Because a batch of 1 costs 5.58 ms and a batch of 64 costs 10.85 ms, each per-row call wastes roughly 5.41 ms of fixed overhead.

H2_small_microbatch_and_per_row_scorer.claim: microbatch_rows=8, per-row conditional scorer and ragged CPU/NumPy transforms dominate the learner.
H2_small_microbatch_and_per_row_scorer.evidence: Learner split: ppo_loop 66.2%, vold_encode 23.2%, vold_obs 4.3%, checkpoint 2.2%, model create 3.3%. The ppo_loop contains the per-row evaluate_encoded path; an earlier isolated split measured it at 52.2% of a single learner evaluation.
H2_small_microbatch_and_per_row_scorer.detail: Per-row scorer evaluation inside ppo_loop plus per-row V_old encode together account for essentially all learner time. Batch 1 vs 64 kernel scaling shows the mechanism is per-call latency amortisation, not arithmetic.

H3_ipc_queue_barrier.claim: InferenceServer ENCODE and prefix STEP IPC/queue/synchronisation barriers dominate collection.
H3_ipc_queue_barrier.evidence: Per request: prep 0.179 ms, submit 0.343 ms, wait 11.792 ms (wait/prep = 65.99x). Direct in-process GPU encode of the same 4 rows: 6.091 ms (1.355 ms/row). Within collection: step_levels 9820.1 ms (62.1%), encode 5109.7 ms (32.3%).
H3_ipc_queue_barrier.detail: The transport path pays 11.792 ms per request while payload prep is 0.179 ms. step_levels + encode are 94.4% of accounted collection, and both are dominated by submit/queue/wait.

H4_instrumentation_in_production_path.claim: Per-forward JSON statistics writes or accidental instrumentation inflate the nominal P4 path.
H4_instrumentation_in_production_path.evidence: PA4_P3_STATS_PATH was unset in the frozen environment (ENVIRONMENT.json thread_env). The profiler is off unless PA4_P45_PROFILE=1, and off-mode tests prove it records nothing and writes no file. The instrumented run (0.5524 m/s over 2 iters) is slightly faster than the uninstrumented median (0.5338 m/s).
H4_instrumentation_in_production_path.detail: No stats-file path is active by default; instrumentation is gated and off-mode is proven inert by 14 negative-control tests.

H5_per_iteration_recreation.claim: Recreating the actor server, frozen critic and reloading optimizer/snapshot files each iteration is a major cost.
H5_per_iteration_recreation.evidence: frozen_model_create 391.8 ms + frozen_state_load 32.3 ms + learner_create 368.3 ms over 2 iterations = ~793 ms, about 3.5% of learner time and ~1.4% of wall.
H5_per_iteration_recreation.detail: Model construction is ~200 ms per call and happens twice per iteration. It is measurable but an order of magnitude smaller than the per-row scoring costs; not a primary cause.

H6_gpu_saturated_needs_faster_gpu.claim: The runtime is GPU-saturated, so a faster GPU helps without architectural change.
H6_gpu_saturated_needs_faster_gpu.evidence: Encode kernel time at batch 1 = 5.583 ms and at batch 64 = 10.85 ms, i.e. 1.94x for 64x the work. Per-row kernel cost falls from 5.583 ms to 0.17 ms. Peak VRAM 496-663 MiB of 8188 MiB. GPU idles at 210 MHz / P8 between calls.
H6_gpu_saturated_needs_faster_gpu.detail: The GPU is not saturated: it is starved. Latency dominates, and a faster card would reduce the fixed ~5 ms kernel latency only partially. The measured lever is batch size, not FLOPS.
